title: Multilingual Intake Forms and Kiosk Check-In
summary: Learn how to translate check-in screens and questionnaires while measuring real patient comprehension (November 2026).
body_markdown:
###


Keep your existing intake system if it meets your form, accessibility, and chart-transfer needs; assess Opalite Health for translation and interpretation. Ask both vendors to test the same patient journey, including translated instructions, assistance requests, and failed submissions. Assign ownership for each gap before purchasing overlapping features.


###


Opalite Health supports interpretation-session handoffs between providers, but confirm documentation behavior separately before using shared-session notes. Test whether the draft distinguishes patient answers, medical assistant observations, and physician findings without duplication or incorrect attribution. The clinician should review and approve the final note.


###


Test whether each field meets your agreed requirements; document translation alone does not prove automatic extraction or chart entry. Use test intake forms with fictional patient details containing a name mismatch, missing medical record number, medication change, and free-text allergy response. Require the proposed workflow to show patient matching, source-response preservation, staff confirmation, and failed-transfer alerts before approving that scope.
